schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE customers
(
    CustomerID INTEGER UNIQUE     not null
        primary key,
    Segment    TEXT null,
    Currency   TEXT null
);

CREATE TABLE gasstations
(
    GasStationID INTEGER    UNIQUE   not null
        primary key,
    ChainID      INTEGER          null,
    Country      TEXT null,
    Segment      TEXT null
);

CREATE TABLE products
(
    ProductID   INTEGER   UNIQUE      not null
        primary key,
    Description TEXT null
);

CREATE TABLE "transactions_1k"
(
    TransactionID INTEGER
        primary key autoincrement,
    Date          DATE,
    Time          TEXT,
    CustomerID    INTEGER,
    CardID        INTEGER,
    GasStationID  INTEGER,
    ProductID     INTEGER,
    Amount        INTEGER,
    Price         REAL
);

CREATE TABLE "yearmonth"
(
    CustomerID  INTEGER not null
        references customers
            on update cascade on delete cascade
        references customers,
    Date        TEXT    not null,
    Consumption REAL,
    primary key (Date, CustomerID)
);
q1: SELECT T2.Description FROM transactions_1k AS T1 INNER JOIN products AS T2 ON T1.ProductID = T2.ProductID ORDER BY T1.Amount DESC LIMIT 5
q2: SELECT p.Description FROM products AS p INNER JOIN "transactions_1k" AS t ON p.ProductID = t.ProductID GROUP BY p.ProductID ORDER BY SUM(t.Amount) DESC LIMIT 5
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT T2.Description FROM transactions_1k AS T1 INNER JOIN products AS T2 ON T1.ProductID = T2.ProductID ORDER BY T1.Amount DESC LIMIT 5
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT p.Description FROM products AS p INNER JOIN "transactions_1k" AS t ON p.ProductID = t.ProductID GROUP BY p.ProductID ORDER BY SUM(t.Amount) DESC LIMIT 5
counterexample: INSERT INTO products (ProductID, Description) VALUES (1, 'Product A'); INSERT INTO transactions_1k (TransactionID, ProductID, Amount) VALUES (1, 1, 100); INSERT INTO transactions_1k (TransactionID, ProductID, Amount) VALUES (2, 1, 10);
explanation: Q1 selects the top 5 products by the highest transaction amount, while Q2 selects the top 5 products by the highest total transaction amount. The difference arises because Q1 orders by the amount of a single transaction, whereas Q2 orders by the sum of all transactions for a product.
counterexample_dsp: Create a scenario where a product has two transactions, one with a high amount and another with a low amount. Q1 will return the product based on the high transaction amount, while Q2 will return it based on the total transaction amount (high + low).
